stories.title: Corpay’s Cross-Border Business Leases Prebuilt at Rudin’s 560 Lexington
stories.excerpt: Rudin announced a new 11-year office lease with Corpay, Inc.’s. Cross-Border business at 560 Lexington Ave., its 22-story office tower in the Plaza District. Corpay Cross-Border Solutions, which specializes in foreign exchange, global payments and risk management, will relocate its headquarters to 560 Lexington this fall. The company will occupy a 17,778-square-foot prebuilt space spanning the entire 17th floor of the 380,000-square-foot building.  “Corpay’s commitment to 560 Lexington demonstrates the continued allure of the Plaza District and further validates our investments in our portfolio’s amenity and pre-build programs. Given these ongoing efforts, only minor modifications to a prebuilt floor were needed to meet Corpay’s requirements. This allowed us to accommodate their accelerated timeline for move-in, which was a big factor in getting the deal done,” said Kevin Daly, Vice President of Office Leasing at Rudin. Jacob Rosenthal and Kevin Carroll of CBRE represented Corpay. Rudin was represented in-house by Kevin Daly and a CBRE team of Peter Turchin, Brett Shannon, Eric Deutsch and Lauren Levy. The post Corpay’s Cross-Border Business Leases Prebuilt at Rudin’s 560 Lexington appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Corpay Cross-Border relocates HQ to 560 Lexington Ave., NYC; 11-year lease, 17,778 sq ft.
Prebuilt office space allowed accelerated move-in; minimal buildout required.
Signal of sustained office leasing in Plaza District despite broader office headwinds.
stories.summary: Corpay, Inc.'s Cross-Border Solutions division signed an 11-year lease for a full 17th-floor prebuilt space (17,778 sq ft) at Rudin's 560 Lexington Avenue in Manhattan, relocating its headquarters there this fall. The company was attracted by the Plaza District's amenities and the availability of a pre-built floor that required only minor modifications, enabling an accelerated timeline. The lease signals continued institutional demand for premium office in Midtown Manhattan despite broader sector challenges.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily impact. This is an office transaction signaling selective corporate investment in Manhattan's Plaza District, which could support adjacent rental housing demand, but the story does not indicate net job creation or population influx—it is likely a lateral relocation. Monitor whether Corpay's move attracts or retains white-collar talent in Manhattan, which would support long-term residential demand in downtown/Midtown submarkets.

stories.title: Marcus & Millichap’s Azzi Group Closes Value-Add Sale of West Hollywood Multifamily
stories.excerpt: Marcus & Millichap closed the sale of 1203 N. Kings Road, a 30-unit multifamily property in West Hollywood. The property sold for $7.98 million, or $266,000 per unit. “The property presented the buyer with a rare opportunity to acquire a well-located West Hollywood asset at an attractive basis with significant value-add potential,” said Tony Azzi, executive managing director investments. “With opportunities to renovate vacant units and improve operations, the buyer is well positioned to enhance the property’s long-term cash flow. West Hollywood continues to benefit from strong rental demand driven by limited housing supply, walkability and access to major employment and lifestyle destinations throughout Los Angeles,” added Rabbie Banafsheha, senior director investments. Azzi and Banafsheha, of The Azzi Group in Marcus & Millichap’s Los Angeles office, had the exclusive listing to market the property on behalf of the seller. Azzi, Banafsheha, Arteen Zahiri and Ian Habbestad, also of The Azzi Group, procured the buyer. The post Marcus & Millichap’s Azzi Group Closes Value-Add Sale of West Hollywood Multifamily appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: 30-unit West Hollywood property sold for $7.98M ($266K/unit); value-add acquisition.
Buyer positioned to renovate vacant units and improve operations.
Strong rental demand in West Hollywood driven by supply scarcity, walkability, employment access.
stories.summary: Marcus & Millichap's Azzi Group closed the sale of 1203 N. Kings Road, a 30-unit multifamily property in West Hollywood, for $7.98 million ($266,000 per unit) to a buyer seeking value-add upside. The asset featured vacant units and operational improvement opportunities. Brokers attributed the transaction to West Hollywood's strong rental demand, limited housing supply, walkability, and proximity to major Los Angeles employment and lifestyle destinations.
stories.impact: West Hollywood submarket remains tight on supply with robust rental demand, validating acquisition prices even at $266K/unit on a value-add basis. For a developer, this signals a window to acquire, renovate, and stabilize assets in LA's Westside; limited new supply competition and demand fundamentals support margin capture through unit renovation and operational lift. Strong performer for capital deployment in Los Angeles.

stories.title: Northmarq Arranges $75M Acquisition Loan for Grocery-Anchored Queens Center
stories.excerpt: Northmarq’s New York Debt + Equity team led by Robert Delitsky and Keith Braddish arranged a $75-million loan for the acquisition and redevelopment of Whitestone Shopping Center, a 119,584-square-foot grocery-anchored shopping center located at 153-17 Cross Island Pkwy. in Whitestone, Queens. Northmarq arranged financing on behalf of BTF Whitestone LLC after running a marketing process with the lending community. Northmarq and ownership selected Acadia Realty Trust. The principals of BTF Whitestone LLC are Aaron Malinsky and Kenneth Schuckman. “After being overlooked for decades, Whitestone Shopping Center is about to undergo a significant transformation that will benefit both its tenants and the surrounding community,” said Delitsky. “Kenneth Schuckman and Aaron Malinsky are the ideal developers to restore Whitestone Shopping Center into a vibrant neighborhood retail destination.” The center is anchored by Key Food Supermarket, with additional tenants including Webster Bank and JPMorgan Chase. The post Northmarq Arranges $75M Acquisition Loan for Grocery-Anchored Queens Center appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Northmarq arranged $75M acquisition loan for Whitestone Shopping Center, Queens; grocery-anchored.
BTF Whitestone LLC (Malinsky, Schuckman) undertaking significant redevelopment/transformation.
Retail property receiving institutional debt support signals capital flowing to neighborhood retail.
stories.summary: Northmarq's New York Debt + Equity team arranged a $75 million acquisition and redevelopment loan for Whitestone Shopping Center (119,584 sq ft, grocery-anchored) in Queens on behalf of BTF Whitestone LLC. The property, anchored by Key Food Supermarket with additional tenants including Webster Bank and JPMorgan Chase, is slated for significant transformation after being "overlooked for decades." Acadia Realty Trust was selected as the lender.
stories.impact: Not directly relevant to multifamily. However, neighborhood-level retail redevelopment and mixed-use activation in Queens (especially Whitestone) can support surrounding residential demand; monitor whether BTF's transformation plan includes residential or workforce housing components that could create adjacent multifamily opportunities or support rental absorption in Queens' far neighborhoods.

stories.title: SRS Arranges Sale of Newly Built Caliber Collision Property
stories.excerpt: SRS Real Estate Partners has completed the $5.24-million sale of a Caliber Collision property located at 742 Main Street in Chula Vista. The 16,832-square-foot property recently completed construction and has a 15-year corporate-guaranteed absolute triple net lease in place. SRS Capital Markets Senior Managing Principals Matthew Mousavi and Patrick Luther and Vice President Greg Labarre represented the seller, a Southern California-based developer.  The buyer was a family trust from Southern California. The property is part of a new development that will feature Starbucks, Quick Quack Car Wash, Taco Bell, Circle K, and Chipotle, among other recognizable brands, all being separately marketed and available for sale by SRS with a total value of approximately $30 million. It is less than one mile from Interstate 805 and Chula Vista Crossings, a Kohl’s-anchored retail center. “This property had a significant amount of investor interest and sold over the asking price, which was a 5.5% cap rate,” said Luther. “This long-term tenant is poised to do significant business as it is located near multiple auto dealerships and auto service retailers and is in a densely populated area with more than 348,200 residents, and 81,200 employees within a one-mile radius.” Mousavi added, “This was an ideal, fee-simple, low-maintenance opportunity for the new owner as it presents minimal property management responsibilities.” The post SRS Arranges Sale of Newly Built Caliber Collision Property appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Caliber Collision property in Chula Vista sold for $5.24M; newly built, 15-year triple-net lease.
Property part of $30M mixed-use development (Starbucks, Quack Quash, Taco Bell, Chipotle, Circle K).
Strong investor interest; cap rate 5.5%; dense market (348K residents, 81K employees within 1 mile).
stories.summary: SRS Real Estate Partners completed the $5.24 million sale of a newly built, 16,832-square-foot Caliber Collision property in Chula Vista, California, with a 15-year corporate-guaranteed absolute triple-net lease. The property is part of a $30 million mixed-use development anchored by national retailers (Starbucks, Quick Quack Car Wash, Taco Bell, Chipotle, Circle K) near Interstate 805. The property sold above asking price at a 5.5% cap rate, indicating robust investor appetite in a dense trade area (348,200 residents, 81,200 employees within one mile).
stories.impact: Not directly multifamily. However, strong retail development and anchor-tenant investment in Chula Vista near I-805 indicates growing retail/employment concentration that supports ancillary residential demand. A developer should monitor whether this retail node and surrounding density will drive workforce housing demand or Class-B/C apartment absorption in the greater Chula Vista/South Bay submarket.

stories.title: NAI Hanson Tapped to Lease former Barnes & Noble Headquarters
stories.excerpt: NAI James E. Hanson announced that SVPs W. Joshua Levering, SIOR, and Charles Laginestra, and associate Chris D’Andrea, have been tapped by First National Realty Management, LLC, as the exclusive leasing team for 120 Mountainview Blvd. in Basking Ridge, NJ. The former world headquarters of Barnes & Noble, 120 Mountainview features a two-story lobby, an onsite cafe, outdoor seating, a bocce court, over 500 on-site parking spaces, and more. The property also offers a location near Interstates 78 and 287, providing access to Newark Liberty International Airport, New York City and Somerset County’s corporate corridor. “This is a rare opportunity to secure a large block of Class-A space in one of the state’s most established corporate corridors,” said Levering. “With new ownership that is experienced and fully committed to reinvesting in the property, 120 Mountainview is perfectly suited for users seeking a striking headquarters that offers flexibility, connectivity, responsive ownership, and a full suite of premium amenities.” The post NAI Hanson Tapped to Lease former Barnes & Noble Headquarters appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: NAI Hanson appointed exclusive leasing team for 120 Mountainview Blvd, Basking Ridge, NJ.
Former Barnes & Noble headquarters; Class-A, 500+ parking, near I-78, I-287, Newark airport.
New ownership committed to reinvestment; marketed as large block corporate headquarters opportunity.
stories.summary: NAI James E. Hanson was tapped as exclusive leasing agent for 120 Mountainview Boulevard in Basking Ridge, New Jersey, the former world headquarters of Barnes & Noble. The Class-A property features a two-story lobby, on-site cafe, outdoor seating, bocce court, and over 500 on-site parking spaces, with convenient access to Interstates 78 and 287, Newark Liberty International Airport, and Somerset County's corporate corridor. New ownership is fully committed to reinvesting in the asset.
stories.impact: Not directly multifamily. However, a change of control and reinvestment in a high-amenity corporate headquarters campus in Somerset County (NJ's established corporate corridor) could signal workplace modernization and potential in-migration of command-and-control functions to New Jersey suburbs. If successful, this could drive white-collar job growth and professional-class housing demand in the surrounding Basking Ridge/Morris County submarket; monitor leasing traction to gauge whether new HQs will relocate to the region.

stories.title: Starwood Lands $483M CMBS Loan to Refi Single-Family Rental Portfolio
stories.excerpt: Barry Sternlicht’s Starwood Asset Management secured a $482.5 million commercial mortgage-backed securities (CMBS) loan to refinance a nearly full single-family rental portfolio located across 10 states. The floating-rate, interest-only financing — which Japan’s Nomura Securities originated — backs 1,749 properties, according to Fitch Ratings. The debt, which is scheduled to mature in August 2028, has three 12-month extension options. The portfolio was just over 96 percent leased in April. On average, the homes span 1,812 square feet and date back to 1992. Starwood Asset Management paid $674 million for the houses, assembling the portfolio between 2021 and 2022. Nearly a third are located in Georgia, followed by nearly a quarter in Arizona and just under 12 percent in Florida. Within Palm Beach County, there are 27 homes, most of which are located in Lake Worth, according to property records. The debt comes as Starwood has been making other multifamily inroads, buying four affordable housing properties across Miami-Dade County just last week for a combined $115 million. For Nomura, the financing marks a sizable loan since re-entering the U.S. market last year after a 27-year hiatus. A division of Nomura Group, one of Japan’s major financial institutions, the firm had helped pioneer the CMBS scheme back in the 1990s. Representatives for Starwood declined to comment, while representatives for Nomura did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Starwood Asset Management refinanced 1,749 single-family rental homes across 10 states; $482.5M CMBS.
Portfolio 96% leased in April; homes average 1,812 sq ft, dating to 1992.
Strong concentration: Georgia (30%), Arizona (24%), Florida (12%); paid $674M in 2021–2022.
stories.summary: Barry Sternlicht's Starwood Asset Management secured a $482.5 million floating-rate, interest-only CMBS loan (originated by Nomura Securities) to refinance a nearly full single-family rental portfolio of 1,749 homes across 10 states. The portfolio was 96% leased in April, with average unit size of 1,812 square feet. Starwood assembled the portfolio between 2021 and 2022 for $674 million, with concentrations in Georgia (30%), Arizona (24%), and Florida (12%). The debt matures in August 2028 with three 12-month extension options.
stories.impact: Institutional capital is actively refinancing and holding large SFR portfolios, signaling confidence in single-family rental demand and cashflow across major markets. For a multifamily developer, this highlights strong competition for renter dollars from the SFR sector, especially in Sun Belt markets (Georgia, Arizona, Florida); rental rate growth may be pressured by supply from both multifamily and SFR. Starwood's simultaneous Miami-Dade affordable housing acquisitions suggest capital also seeking density and value-add in multifamily—watch for competing bids in Florida gateway markets.

stories.title: Extell Finalizes Deal to Buy 110 East 55th Street for $65M
stories.excerpt: After months of negotiations, Extell Development has acquired 110 East 55th Street, a 19-story Midtown office property also known as Park 55, from the Parkoff Organization for $65 million, property records made public Monday show. An affiliate of construction company JT Magen — which had previously partnered with Extell on a foreclosure in Boston — filed a pre-foreclosure suit at the property in May, The Real Deal reported. The foreclosure complaint alleged that Parkoff defaulted on a loan and owed some $40.6 million in principal and interest. Parkoff and Extell did not immediately respond to Commercial Observer’s requests for comment. Extell founder Gary Barnett was reported to be in contract for the property back in January, but a sales price was never reported until the deal closed this week. Now, Barnett will add the building to his firm’s ever-growing collection of Midtown-based assets. Most recently, Extell acquired a block-long development site at 405-417 Park Avenue in May for $500 million, CO previously reported. The site — which has the potential for upwards of 700,000 square feet of rentable office space — went up for sale in August of last year. Extell also acquired the Friars Club building at 57 East 55th Street for $19 million in late April. Additionally, Barnett secured 123,000 square feet of air rights over Saint Thomas Church at 678 Fifth Avenue for $36 million last year. It’s unclear exactly what Barnett has planned for his massive Midtown assemblage — which is also set to include 111 East 54th Street — but the developer is already busy with other development projects in Manhattan. The firm has several Midtown developments in the works, including a 600-foot-tall office tower at 570 Fifth Avenue, a 1,200-foot residential tower at 77 West 66th Street, a 70-story condominium at 50 West 66th Street, a 71-story mixed-use tower at 871 Seventh Avenue — the former Wellington Hotel — and a 1,162-foot-tall residential skyscraper at 655 Madison Avenue. bullets: Extell Development acquired 110 East 55th Street (Park 55), Midtown Manhattan, for $65M from Parkoff.
19-story office property; Parkoff defaulted on $40.6M loan; pre-foreclosure suit filed May.
Extell also acquired 405–417 Park Avenue block for $500M (May); building up Midtown portfolio.
stories.summary: Extell Development finalized the acquisition of 110 East 55th Street (Park 55), a 19-story Midtown office building, from the Parkoff Organization for $65 million after months of negotiations. An affiliate of construction company JT Magen filed a pre-foreclosure suit in May, with allegations that Parkoff defaulted on a loan and owed approximately $40.6 million in principal and interest. The deal adds to Extell's growing Midtown real estate portfolio, which recently included the $500 million acquisition of a development site at 405–417 Park Avenue in May.
stories.impact: Extell's aggressive Midtown acquisition spree—including a distressed office buy and a major development site—signals confidence in the firm's ability to convert or redevelop office into residential (or mixed-use) in a high-cost, supply-constrained Manhattan submarket. This activity may presage significant residential pipeline development in Midtown; monitor zoning, approval timelines, and Extell's public statements on residential conversion or new-build plans to anticipate supply influx and competitive positioning in the Manhattan rental market.

stories.title: Terreno Realty Acquires Red Hook Warehouse for $26M
stories.excerpt: Terreno Realty has acquired a warehouse along the Red Hook, Brooklyn, waterfront. Terreno announced Monday the purchase of the 28,000-square-foot industrial property at 659 Court Street for $26.3 million from California-based LBA Properties, which made a pretty penny since buying it less thana year and a half ago for $7 million, according to property records. The building sits right on the banks of the East River with parking for 70 cars and two loading bays, according to the buyers. The warehouse is also leased to a maritime goods and services provider. It’s unclear who brokered the deal. LBA did not immediately respond to a request for comment, while Terreno did not immediately respond to a request for additional comment. With 145,800 square feet of buildable space with the addition of air rights, the price for the property has fluctuated dramatically over the years. Buckeye Partners, which sold the property to LBA in March 2025, acquired it themselves in 2013 for $15.5 million, but paid $92.1 million in a real property transfer tax in late 2019, according to property records. The transaction follows on strong leasing fundamentals reported in the industrial sector in the second quarter of 2026. CBRE clocked leasing at an 11 percent increase year-over-year to 268.7 million square feet across the U.S., while vacancies dropped to 6.5 percent, according to the report. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Terreno Realty acquired Red Hook waterfront warehouse (28K sq ft) for $26.3M; East River location.
LBA Properties flipped asset in <18 months; bought for $7M, sold for $26.3M.
Industrial property with 70 parking spaces, two loading bays; leased to maritime services provider.
stories.summary: Terreno Realty purchased a 28,000-square-foot waterfront warehouse at 659 Court Street in Red Hook, Brooklyn, for $26.3 million. The property sits on the East River, includes parking for 70 cars and two loading bays, and is leased to a maritime goods and services provider. The seller, LBA Properties, acquired the asset less than 18 months prior for $7 million, realizing substantial appreciation. The property includes 145,800 square feet of buildable space with air-rights potential.
stories.impact: Terreno's waterfront Red Hook acquisition, combined with LBA's aggressive flip, signals strong institutional investor appetite for industrial Brooklyn real estate—particularly waterfront assets with development/air-rights upside. For a multifamily developer, Red Hook's trajectory as a mixed-use, residential-friendly waterfront neighborhood is well-established; however, rapid industrial-land appreciation suggests competing uses and potential zoning/land-cost pressure. Monitor whether Terreno or competing buyers convert industrial parcels to residential—this could unlock significant residential supply in an underserved, high-demand Brooklyn micromarket.

stories.title: Aircraft Finance Firm Buys Florida HQ Complex For $118M
stories.excerpt: A publicly traded aircraft finance firm has paid $118 million for a three-building, 375,000-square-foot campus under construction in Coconut Creek, Fla. disclosed the transaction and purchase price in a public filing this month. The Coconut Creek-based company bought Cocomar Business Park, under development at 4733, 4763 and 4851 West Atlantic Boulevard as its new corporate headquarters, the South Florida Business Journal reported. The company lists its current headquarters as 4700 Lyons Technology Parkway. The seller is an affiliate of Greystar of Charleston, S.C., which last year bought the site for $30.5 million. A marketing brochure said the industrial buildings include 32-foot ceilings, 78 dock doors and 313 parking spaces. Each building includes a small amount of office space and conference rooms. Completion of the 35-acre campus is expected in the third quarter of this year. In its most recent annual report, Willis Lease Finance said it owns its 60,000-square-foot headquarters in Coconut Creek and leases 45,000 square feet in Pompano Beach, Fla., and 25,000 square feet in Sunrise, Fla. The company reported 475 employees in the U.S., the United Kingdom, Ireland and elsewhere. As of the end of 2025, Willis Lease Finance owned 363 engines, 20 aircraft, one marine vessel and other leased parts and equipment leased out to 69 lessees in 37 countries. Jeff Ostrowski can be reached at jostrowski@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Willis Lease Finance Corp. purchased Cocomar Business Park, Coconut Creek, FL, for $118M; new HQ.
Three-building, 375K sq ft campus under construction; 35-acre site; completion Q3 2025.
Greystar (seller) purchased site ~1 year prior for $30.5M; significant appreciation.
stories.summary: Willis Lease Finance Corporation, a publicly traded aircraft finance firm, purchased Cocomar Business Park, a three-building, 375,000-square-foot campus under development in Coconut Creek, Florida, for $118 million as its new corporate headquarters. The 35-acre development (at 4733, 4763, and 4851 West Atlantic Boulevard) includes 32-foot ceilings, 78 dock doors, 313 parking spaces, and modest office/conference space. Completion is expected in Q3 2025. The seller, an affiliate of Greystar, had acquired the site approximately one year prior for $30.5 million.
stories.impact: Corporate headquarters relocation from leased Pompano Beach/Lyons Technology Park to new Cocomar facility signals job consolidation and potential in-migration of back-office and professional staff to the greater Coconut Creek corridor. This supports rental housing demand in northwest Broward County and the broader Miami metro; monitor whether Willis Lease's move attracts additional corporate campuses to the West Atlantic Boulevard corridor, which would drive workforce housing demand and justify multifamily development in underserved Coconut Creek/Sunrise/Margate submarkets.

stories.title: PGIM Sells Delray Beach Assisted Living Community for at Least $140M
stories.excerpt: PGIM Real Estate sold a relatively new assisted living facility in Delray Beach, Fla., for at least $140 million, marking one of the biggest South Florida retirement home sales in recent years. Chevy Chase, Md.-based Artemis Real Estate Partners purchased the 7.2-acre asset, property records show. The 224,951-square-foot community, called The Arbor at Delray, houses 207 apartments at 6595 Morikami Park Road, just west of South Jog Road. The complex includes a 35,586-square-foot recreational clubhouse and a 51,461-square-foot nursing home. The sale breaks down to just under $676,300 per unit, though it’s unclear whether the $140 million figure listed on the deed also includes the operations for the business, which could boost the price tag. PGIM Real Estate, part of insurance giant Prudential Financial, completed the property in 2023. Two years earlier, PGIM-backed Alliance Residential Company purchased the land for $8.2 million and secured a $45.7 million construction loan from Dallas-based Comerica Bank, The Real Deal reported. There’s been an uptick in the number of assisted living facilities across Palm Beach County this year as the occupancy rate in Florida neared 90 percent, with monthly rents averaging over $5,000 in the second quarter of 2026, according to data from Colliers. Just last week, Healthpeak Properties bought a 136-unit facility in Boynton Beach for at least $62 million. Representatives for Artemis and PGIM did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: PGIM Real Estate sold The Arbor at Delray Beach assisted-living facility for ≥$140M.
207-unit community (224,951 sq ft); ~$676K per unit; Artemis Real Estate Partners buyer.
PGIM completed property in 2023; strong institutional exit pricing in Florida senior housing.
stories.summary: PGIM Real Estate sold The Arbor at Delray Beach, a relatively new assisted-living facility, for at least $140 million to Artemis Real Estate Partners (Chevy Chase, Maryland). The 7.2-acre asset at 6595 Morikami Park Road houses 207 apartments plus a 35,586-square-foot recreational clubhouse and 51,461-square-foot nursing home, totaling 224,951 square feet. The transaction breaks down to approximately $676,300 per unit, marking one of the largest South Florida retirement home sales in recent years. PGIM completed the property in 2023.
stories.impact: Strong institutional exit pricing on a recently stabilized senior-housing asset signals robust demand and valuation support in the South Florida retirement/assisted-living sector. For a multifamily developer, this validates the addressable market for age-restricted and senior-focused residential communities in high-growth Florida markets (Delray Beach, Palm Beach County). However, note the differentiated per-unit pricing (~$676K for seniors vs. market multifamily) and operating complexity; consider whether senior housing or assisted-living layered into a mixed-use development could diversify revenue or enhance stabilization in Delray/South County.
